2026-10-15 daily batch A, WRITTEN BY THE CHAIRMAN and fired at session open before the research analyst was convened, for the reason the 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14 batches were fired early: the relay runs on a GitHub runner and its latency is not under this session's control, so a batch committed after a seat's return risks landing after the record closes.

WHAT QUESTION THIS BATCH WAS DESIGNED AGAINST, AND IT WAS PRE-REGISTERED ON MAIN BEFORE THIS SESSION EXISTED. analytics/daily-research/2026-10-14.md next-steps item 5 reads, verbatim: "sha256 MOVED ON A PAGE WHOSE BYTE COUNT DID NOT, ACROSS 24h25m, AND THE BRACKET IS MEASURED: stable across 34 minutes and four runs on /annulment; changed across 24h25m on the Manifest register. So the pages are not per-request salted and the varying element has a timescale between those bounds. A successor wanting to narrow it needs one row at an intermediate interval, and it is cheap." This batch is the first half of that one row, and batch B at this session's close is the second half. The design is fixed by that committed sentence; this file only selects the URLs and the literal that satisfy it.

THIS IS NOT THE FINGERPRINT CADENCE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS IT. The cadence adopted yesterday is six rows a cycle NEXT DUE ON OR AROUND 2026-11-13. Today is not that date and this batch does not advance or reset it. The two share a row shape and nothing else: the cadence asks whether a register's content changed between cycles; this batch asks, against an unchanged register, how fast the non-byte-bearing element of the page varies. Conflating them would let a null here be read as a cadence result.

WHY SIX ROWS RATHER THAN THE TWO THE QUESTION STRICTLY NEEDS. The bracket's two endpoints were measured on two different registers - the 34-minute stability on /annulment, the 24h25m movement on the Manifest register - so a two-row design would leave open whether the difference is the interval or the register. Six rows fingerprint all six certified addresses at one instant, which (a) makes the A-to-B interval comparison a six-way observation rather than a one-way one, and (b) yields, free, a second-day replication of yesterday's 24h25m result against the baselines recorded at next-steps item 2, on all six registers rather than one. Neither of those costs an extra batch.

THE BASELINES THIS BATCH IS READ AGAINST, copied from analytics/daily-research/2026-10-14.md next-steps item 2 and NOT restated from memory, sha256 truncated there to 16 hex characters as it is here: manifest 95,993 / c7c8bb13a7dcf196 (2026-10-14T11:55:39Z); place-of-arbitration 91,430 / afc044a19d09cc6d; disqualification 116,531 / eee50c4a9106e8d2; ndp 121,557 / e4cd72acc514d561; annulment 121,583 / 6f3b9357466a642c; provisional-measures 161,240 / cb7d36d541d555d5. The interval will be computed from the timestamps the reductions themselves carry, not from the session clock.

WHAT A ROW BELOW FOUNDS: that the path resolved at the batch instant with the status recorded, and the byte length and sha256 of what the runner received. NOTHING ELSE. No row below founds any entry, party, designator, date, disposition, holding, ground or outcome in any of the six registers; 400 characters is no reading of a register. A byte count and a digest are facts about a retrieved octet stream, not about a table's contents, and a digest that moves is not evidence that any entry changed.

WHY THE LITERAL IS NAVIGATION CHROME AND NOT A REGISTER'S HEADING. Every row's find is "In this section", which is attested in visible prose on this host across all six certified addresses by this project's own reductions of 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14. It is used here so that each row returns a non-empty window and therefore demonstrates that the tag-strip yielded prose from that document - the relay README's requirement that a row expected to null carry a companion control is satisfied structurally instead, because this literal is expected to HIT. Its weakness is stated rather than left implicit: navigation chrome also renders on error pages, so a TRUE here does not establish that the register page was reached - status and final_url do that work.

STANDING QUALIFICATIONS. excerpt_of strips script and style bodies and then every remaining tag before the search runs (scripts/fetch_relay.py:78-79, 126-131), so markup, attributes and hrefs are unreachable to any find; on a miss it returns the empty string rather than a head excerpt (:132-133); the relay does not decode HTML entities, and the one literal used below contains none. A FALSE on any row with a 200 would void that row's reading and would be recorded as an instrument observation, never as a statement about the register.

NO CADENCED ITEM IS DUE TODAY. Thread 11's relay limb was discharged 2026-10-13 and re-anchored to 2026-11-13; its search limb is due on or around 2026-10-25; the standing-dockets thread resumes 2026-10-18. No row below is a search, none carries the Wingtech or Yuching designators, and none is a right-edge-advance row on any register.

THIS COMMIT CARRIES NO SKIP MARKER, per the relay README's rule on skip markers and the narrow rule adopted at analytics/daily-research/2026-10-14.md section 3f.3. It was checked by command before the push rather than diagnosed after a silence. Expect the eventual merge to re-fire this workflow and overwrite the result file in place, as observed on 2026-10-14; the reduction is therefore cited by blob in the record, and the re-fire is itself a free third time point.
